On the other hand, Hsp27 can act as a chaperone and modulate signaling pathways. Hsp27 has been shown to inhibit JNK activation under stress conditions. Given that we are looking at phosphoprotein levels, "jnk12" likely refers to the phosphorylated (active) forms of JNK1 and JNK2. Similarly, "hsp27" likely refers to phosphorylated Hsp27. So the question is: Does phosphorylated Hsp27 affect phosphorylated JNK, or vice versa?
